title: Secure a new car battery's hold-down: hook both J-bolts blind into the tray's slots, then fit the bar over them
instruction: Secure the battery with its hold-down: hook each J-bolt into its slot in the battery tray, then lay the bar across the battery's top with both bolts through its slots.
context: Fitting a new car battery is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023.00; about 825,800 US jobs, 2025). The battery must be held down before the car is driven: a loose one shifts, can short its terminals against the hood or body and crack its case. Hold-down kits are fitted this way: hook each J-bolt into its slot in the tray, then lay the bar across the battery over both bolts (Dorman hold-down kit instructions). The hooks catch 21 cm down beside the battery, out of sight, and a hooked bolt let go leans and can slip back out, so both must stay hooked while the bar goes on.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Engine bay: a hole 34 x 28 cm in the table (x 13.0 to 47.0, y -14.0 to 14.0) over a dark steel well whose floor is 20.65 cm below the table top. Battery: a BCI Group 35 car battery, 23.0 x 17.5 x 22.5 cm (black polypropylene case, two lead posts), its length along x, centred at (30.0, 0.0), its top 4.0 cm above the table; seated in its tray (about 17 kg). Tray: black-coated steel, its floor 2 mm thick spanning x 18.0 to 42.0, y -10.6 to 10.6, carried 1.95 cm above the well's floor on a steel bracket under the battery (x 19.0 to 41.0, y -8.0 to 8.0); in the floor, halfway along each long side of the battery, a hook slot 28 x 10 mm (x 28.6 to 31.4, |y| 9.0 to 10.0); 4 cm side walls at |y| 10.6 and end walls at x 18.0 and 42.0. J-bolts: two zinc-plated steel J-bolts, 1/4 in (6.35 mm) rod, 30.5 cm from the hook's underside to the top, the hook's tip 12.4 mm from the shank and 18 mm tall, 80 g each; each stands hook down, tip towards +x, in an orange plastic holder 3 x 3 x 6 cm (a 20 x 7 mm slot through it) on the well's floor, the shanks at (14.9, 11.2) and (14.9, -11.2). Bar: black-coated steel hold-down bar 22.8 x 2.54 x 0.4 cm, 170 g, a slot 10 x 20 mm (long along the bar) centred 9.6 cm either side of its middle; it lies flat on the table along x, centred at (30.0, -25.0).
scoring: Tools: a ruler and a phone level. Hooked: a J-bolt's shank passes through its slot in the tray and its hook's tip is under the tray's floor past the slot's edge, so that lifting the bolt by its top it stops against the tray. Bar on: the bar lies on the battery's top (no gap over 3 mm), within 5 degrees of level, with each bolt up through a different one of its two slots. At the end: 0 if neither bolt is hooked; 0.25 if one is; 0.5 if both are but the bar is not on with both bolts through its slots; 0.75 if both are hooked and the bar is on, but the robot still touches a bolt or the bar; 1.0 the same with the robot off them, held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand both J-bolts back hook down in their holders, tips towards +x, and lay the bar back on the table as in the setup.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX at 240 Hz with the parts' real sizes and masses: a BCI Group 35 battery (about 17 kg) seated in a steel tray, two 80 g zinc-plated steel 1/4 in J-bolts 30.5 cm long, a 170 g steel bar, steel-on-steel friction. The hook's catch under the tray's floor, the slots and the bar's slotted ends are modelled to the millimetre, so a hook a few mm out of line lands on the tray instead of going through. Contacts are rigid: the steel bar and bolts do not flex.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the right arm picked the bar up near one end and carried it about over the battery but never laid it down; the left arm stayed near its start; neither arm went to the J-bolts, which stayed in their holders); demo: 1.0
